emergent imaging is not necessary in patients with Sturg-Weber syndrome presenting with seizures, but it is necessary in patients presenting with strokelike symptoms or headaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients presenting with strokelike events or headaches should be considered for emergent imaging, whereas those with breakthrough seizures may be safely managed without emergent neuroimaging.
patients with Sturges-Weber Syndrome should have a thorough neurologic evaluation and not undergo emergent neuroimaging if they present with seizures.

patients with Sturg-Weber syndrome with acute neurologic complaints should be managed conservatively, with a low threshold for emergent imaging, but with a high index of clinical suspicion for other etiologies of acute neurologic symptoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
emergent brain imaging in patients with Sturg-Weber syndrome is unlikely to reveal acute hemorrhagic or thrombotic events.
emergent imaging is not warranted for patients with Sturge Weber Syndrome presenting with breakthrough seizures.
patients with Sturgeweber syndrome presenting with acute neurologic complaints are frequently imaged, but these imaging studies are often negative and do not change management.
